state.information_rules: Opponent sets and pending action are unknown. Move power is base power, not calculated damage. Public HP is rounded. Effect counters are official client data, not guaranteed remaining durations.

heavydutyboots.name: Heavy-Duty Boots
heavydutyboots.desc: When switching in, the holder is unaffected by hazards on its side of the field.

leftovers.name: Leftovers
leftovers.desc: At the end of every turn, holder restores 1/16 of its max HP.

souldew.name: Soul Dew
souldew.desc: If held by a Latias/Latios, its Dragon- and Psychic-type moves have 1.2x power.

toxicorb.name: Toxic Orb
toxicorb.desc: At the end of every turn, this item attempts to badly poison the holder.

dauntlessshield.name: Dauntless Shield
dauntlessshield.desc: On switch-in, this Pokemon's Defense is raised by 1 stage. Once per battle.

levitate.name: Levitate
levitate.desc: This Pokemon is immune to Ground-type attacks and the effects of Spikes, Toxic Spikes, Sticky Web, and the Arena Trap Ability. The effects of Gravity, Ingrain, Smack Down, Thousand Arrows, and Iron Ball nullify the immunity. Thousand Arrows can hit this Pokemon as if it did not have this Ability.

poisonheal.name: Poison Heal
poisonheal.desc: If this Pokemon is poisoned, it restores 1/8 of its maximum HP, rounded down, at the end of each turn instead of losing HP.

poisonpuppeteer.name: Poison Puppeteer
poisonpuppeteer.desc: If this Pokemon is a Pecharunt and poisons or badly poisons a target, the target also becomes confused.

tintedlens.name: Tinted Lens
tintedlens.desc: This Pokemon's attacks that are not very effective on a target deal double damage.

vesselofruin.name: Vessel of Ruin
vesselofruin.desc: Active Pokemon without this Ability have their Special Attack multiplied by 0.75.

closecombat.name: Close Combat
closecombat.desc: Lowers the user's Defense and Special Defense by 1 stage.

crunch.name: Crunch
crunch.desc: Has a 20% chance to lower the target's Defense by 1 stage.

dracometeor.name: Draco Meteor
dracometeor.desc: Lowers the user's Special Attack by 2 stages.

earthquake.name: Earthquake
earthquake.desc: Damage doubles if the target is using Dig.

firstimpression.name: First Impression
firstimpression.desc: Fails unless it is the user's first turn on the field.

flipturn.name: Flip Turn
flipturn.desc: If this move is successful and the user has not fainted, the user switches out even if it is trapped and is replaced immediately by a selected party member. The user does not switch out if there are no unfainted party members, or if the target switched out using an Eject Button or through the effect of the Emergency Exit or Wimp Out Abilities.

foulplay.name: Foul Play
foulplay.desc: Damage is calculated using the target's Attack stat, including stat stage changes. The user's Ability, item, and burn are used as normal.

icefang.name: Ice Fang
icefang.desc: Has a 10% chance to freeze the target and a 10% chance to make it flinch.

knockoff.name: Knock Off
knockoff.desc: If the target is holding an item that can be removed from it, ignoring the Sticky Hold Ability, this move's power is multiplied by 1.5. If the user has not fainted, the target loses its held item. This move cannot cause Pokemon with the Sticky Hold Ability to lose their held item or cause a Kyogre, a Groudon, a Giratina, an Arceus, a Genesect, a Silvally, a Zacian, or a Zamazenta to lose their Blue Orb, Red Orb, Griseous Orb, Plate, Drive, Memory, Rusted Sword, or Rusted Shield respectively. Items lost to this move cannot be regained with Recycle or the Harvest Ability.

malignantchain.name: Malignant Chain
malignantchain.desc: Has a 50% chance to badly poison the target.

partingshot.name: Parting Shot
partingshot.desc: Lowers the target's Attack and Special Attack by 1 stage. If this move is successful, the user switches out even if it is trapped and is replaced immediately by a selected party member. The user does not switch out if the target's Attack and Special Attack stat stages were both unchanged, or if there are no unfainted party members.

protect.name: Protect
protect.desc: The user is protected from most attacks made by other Pokemon during this turn. This move has a 1/X chance of being successful, where X starts at 1 and triples each time this move is successfully used. X resets to 1 if this move fails, if the user's last move used is not Baneful Bunker, Burning Bulwark, Detect, Endure, King's Shield, Max Guard, Obstruct, Protect, Quick Guard, Silk Trap, Spiky Shield, or Wide Guard, or if it was one of those moves and the user's protection was broken. Fails if the user moves last this turn.

psychicnoise.name: Psychic Noise
psychicnoise.desc: For 2 turns, the target is prevented from restoring any HP as long as it remains active. During the effect, healing and draining moves are unusable, and Abilities and items that grant healing will not heal the user. If an affected Pokemon uses Baton Pass, the replacement will remain unable to restore its HP. Pain Split and the Regenerator Ability are unaffected.

recover.name: Recover
recover.desc: The user restores 1/2 of its maximum HP, rounded half up.

ruination.name: Ruination
ruination.desc: Deals damage to the target equal to half of its current HP, rounded down, but not less than 1 HP.

spikes.name: Spikes
spikes.desc: Sets up a hazard on the opposing side of the field, damaging each opposing Pokemon that switches in, unless it is a Flying-type Pokemon or has the Levitate Ability. Can be used up to three times before failing. Opponents lose 1/8 of their maximum HP with one layer, 1/6 of their maximum HP with two layers, and 1/4 of their maximum HP with three layers, all rounded down. Can be removed from the opposing side if any Pokemon uses Tidy Up, or if any opposing Pokemon uses Mortal Spin, Rapid Spin, or Defog successfully, or is hit by Defog.

stealthrock.name: Stealth Rock
stealthrock.desc: Sets up a hazard on the opposing side of the field, damaging each opposing Pokemon that switches in. Fails if the effect is already active on the opposing side. Foes lose 1/32, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, or 1/2 of their maximum HP, rounded down, based on their weakness to the Rock type; 0.25x, 0.5x, neutral, 2x, or 4x, respectively. Can be removed from the opposing side if any Pokemon uses Tidy Up, or if any opposing Pokemon uses Mortal Spin, Rapid Spin, or Defog successfully, or is hit by Defog.

stoneedge.name: Stone Edge
stoneedge.desc: Has a higher chance for a critical hit.

suckerpunch.name: Sucker Punch
suckerpunch.desc: Fails if the target did not select a physical attack, special attack, or Me First for use this turn, or if the target moves before the user.

uturn.name: U-turn
uturn.desc: If this move is successful and the user has not fainted, the user switches out even if it is trapped and is replaced immediately by a selected party member. The user does not switch out if there are no unfainted party members, or if the target switched out using an Eject Button or through the effect of the Emergency Exit or Wimp Out Abilities.

whirlwind.name: Whirlwind
whirlwind.desc: The target is forced to switch out and be replaced with a random unfainted ally. Fails if the target is the last unfainted Pokemon in its party, or if the target used Ingrain previously or has the Suction Cups Ability.

action.instructions:
Choose exactly one legal candidate that best improves the controlled side's chance of winning this Generation 9 OU singles battle. Compare all available moves and switches. Balance immediate offensive value with survival, positioning, status, hazards, remaining team roles, and conservation or timely use of Terastallization. A Terastallization candidate means Terastallize and use that move in the same turn; an ordinary move candidate does not spend Terastallization.
Use the current state as authoritative. The opponent's unrevealed moves, ability, item, stats and pending action are unknown; never treat guesses as observed facts. Base power is not calculated damage. Take move priority, speed changes, immunities and accuracy into account without assuming guaranteed outcomes. Public opponent HP is rounded. Recent completed-turn events are history, not a replacement for the current state.
For forced switches, choose the best next Pokemon among the supplied switch candidates. The candidate IDs identify exact request slots; use their descriptions and the team slot numbers to identify the intended action. All candidates are legal for this request. Select the best available candidate even if every option is unfavorable. No free-text explanation or tool call is required.

State value semantics: unknown means evidence is unavailable, not zero or absence. Empty boosts means all boost stages are zero; empty volatiles/turnstatuses/movestatuses means no such effects. Empty status means known absence of a major status. status_data contains observed client counters, not guaranteed remaining duration. For the controlled team, teraType is the configured Tera type; terastallized and tera_type describe the applied Terastallization type, with an empty string meaning not yet Terastallized. Do not treat teraType as an already applied type. At team preview, active in the private request is a request slot flag, not a lead that has already entered battle. Initial state values are supplied only at a verified prebattle boundary. current_pp_reason explains unknown PP. Do not infer unknown PP from base move power or from the configured Tera type.

state.effect_reference contains general Generation 9 rules for referenced items, abilities, and moves, keyed by normalized ID with name and full desc. Descriptions are not evidence that an opponent possesses or has activated an effect. Apply them only to confirmed or supplied state; do not infer unrevealed opponent sets from this dictionary.

GENERATION 9 SINGLES MECHANICS

Apply standard Pokemon Scarlet/Violet Generation 9 singles mechanics.

Major status:
- Burn: 1/16 max HP residual damage each turn and normally halves physical damage dealt.
- Paralysis: Speed is halved and each attempted action has a 25% chance of full paralysis.
- Poison: 1/8 max HP residual damage each turn.
- Toxic poison: damage increases each turn from 1/16, 2/16, 3/16, etc.; the Toxic counter resets on switching.
- Sleep: normally prevents actions for 1-3 sleep turns, subject to moves such as Sleep Talk.
- Freeze: normally prevents actions and has a 20% natural thaw chance each turn; some moves can thaw immediately.
- A Pokemon normally cannot have more than one major status condition at once.
- Confusion is volatile and disappears on switching.

Relevant type immunities include Fire to burn, Electric to paralysis, Poison/Steel to poison, Ice to freeze, and Grass to powder/spore moves, unless an explicit effect overrides the normal interaction.

Stat stages range from -6 to +6. +1 = 1.5x, +2 = 2x, -1 = 2/3x, and -2 = 1/2x. Most stat stages and volatile conditions reset when switching.

Move order is determined by priority first, then effective Speed. Do not assume a faster base Speed moves first if priority, paralysis, Choice Scarf, boosts, weather, or other effects alter the order.

Damage depends on more than base power. Account for attacking and defensive stats, stat stages, STAB, type effectiveness, abilities, items, weather, terrain, critical hits, and damage rolls.

Entry hazards:
- Stealth Rock damages switch-ins according to their Rock weakness/resistance; neutral damage is 1/8 max HP.
- Spikes damage grounded switch-ins: 1 layer = 1/8, 2 = 1/6, 3 = 1/4.
- Toxic Spikes poison grounded switch-ins; two layers badly poison them.
- Sticky Web lowers the Speed of grounded switch-ins by one stage.
- Heavy-Duty Boots normally prevent entry-hazard effects.

Switching normally removes stat changes, confusion, Substitute, and many other volatile effects, but HP loss and major status remain.

Weather, terrain, screens, hazards, residual damage, recovery, item removal, and field duration must be considered when evaluating future turns.

Each side may Terastallize once per battle. Terastallization changes defensive typing to the Tera type and can alter offensive STAB. Treat unused Tera as a limited strategic resource, not merely an immediate damage boost.

Do not assume unknown opponent moves, items, abilities, EVs, Tera type, or future actions. Apply special abilities, items, and move-specific exceptions only when they are confirmed or otherwise supplied by the battle state.
